claims.text: MAX_CONTENT_CHARS = 200_000 -- Fail-closed ceiling on a single turn. Transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); the per-council budget lives in session.py, but no single turn may blow the file up on its own.
claims.why: Claim about growth complexity and budget in session.py cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: _ACTOR_RE = re.compile(r"^council\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*\.[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+-]*$") -- ADR-010 actor-namespace rule, pinned to the MODEL and not just the vendor: "claude said X" is not reproducible six months out, because the model behind a stable command name changes underneath it.
claims.why: Claim about ADR-010 and reproducibility cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: _NON_BODY_FIELDS = frozenset({"ts", "prev", "entry_sha", "id", "body_sha"}) -- Position/identity fields, excluded from body_sha (see module docstring).
claims.why: Claim about module docstring cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: _ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS = frozenset({...}) -- Accepted caller keys. A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body and hands the caller a success id for a turn never recorded.
claims.why: Claim about refusal behaviour cannot be verified from this chunk; no enforcement code shown.

claims.text: _APPEND_CACHE: dict[str, dict] = {} -- Per-store append index: tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, keyed by resolved path and invalidated by the file's (size, mtime_ns). Re-parsing the whole transcript per append is O(n^2) overall; a 500-turn council must not pay that.
claims.why: Claim about cache invalidation and complexity cannot be verified from this chunk; no usage shown.

claims.text: canonical_body(record: dict) -> dict -- The content projection ``body_sha`` is taken over: everything EXCEPT the position/identity fields. Uniform across turn and roster records so the chain walk needs no per-record-type branch.
claims.why: Function returns dict excluding _NON_BODY_FIELDS as claimed.

claims.text: canonical_body_json(record: dict) -> str -- The exact bytes hashed. Exposed so a test can assert determinism against the canonical form rather than against a digest it cannot inspect.
claims.why: Function returns JSON string of canonical body with sorted keys and no whitespace, as claimed.

claims.text: _entry_sha(prev: str | None, body_sha: str, ts: str) -> str -- payload = (prev or "") + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts
actor_id(vendor: str, model: str) -> str -- ``council.<vendor>.<model>`` per ADR-010. An unknown model id is recorded as the literal ``unknown`` by the CALLER -- never omitted, never inferred.
claims.why: Claim about caller behaviour and 'unknown' literal cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: evidence_ref(path: str, data: bytes) -> dict -- One evidence citation: the path as given plus the sha256 of the exact bytes shown to the model. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: Function returns dict with path (with backslash replacement) and sha256 of data as claimed.

claims.text: council_store_path(council_id: str, base_dir: str | Path | None = None) -> Path -- ``<base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl``. ``council_id`` is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: Function calls _check_council_id and returns Path with council_id.jsonl in base_dir.

claims.text: anchor_path(store_path: str | Path) -> Path -- The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: Function returns Path with .anchor.json suffix as claimed.

claims.text: _check_council_id(council_id: str) -> None -- if not isinstance(council_id, str) or not _COUNCIL_ID_RE.match(council_id): raise ValueError

_resolve_store(council_id: str, store_path: str | Path | None) -> Path -- Resolve and REFUSE any path under ``<repo>/memory/``. Council turns must never reach the memory ledger (see module docstring).
claims.why: Function body incomplete; memory/ refusal logic not fully shown. Claim about module docstring cannot be verified.

observations.what: DEFAULT_COUNCIL_DIR is referenced in council_store_path but not defined in this chunk.
_resolve_store function is incomplete; it ends with a try: block and no except or further code.

_check_council_id is defined after its usage in council_store_path; in Python this is fine as long as the function is called at runtime after definition, but if called during module import (e.g., in a default argument) it would fail.
MAX_CONTENT_CHARS is a hard-coded constant; no mechanism to override it is provided.
evidence_ref replaces backslashes with forward slashes; this may alter paths that already use forward slashes (no-op) but is correct for Windows paths.
canonical_body_json uses json.dumps with sort_keys=True, which guarantees key order but may produce different output for non-string keys or custom types; however, body keys are strings.
